newsitem.title: USA: Caterpillar Q3 EPS seen up about 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Caterpillar Q3 EPS seen up about 30 pct.

text.p: Caterpillar Inc, the world's largest construction and mining equipment maker, is expected by analysts to post a third quarter earnings per share increase of about 30 percent Tuesday, with North American demand helping the gains.
"They have indicated that demand is one of the principal things that's really helping right now, particularly in North America," said J. Blair Brumley, analyst at Dain Bosworth Inc.
The mean estimate of 21 brokers surveyed by First Call is $1.34 a share, compared with $1.07 a share earned in the third quarter of 1995. Estimates range from $1.10 to $1.70.

In the first six months of 1996, Peoria, Illinois-based Caterpillar reported earnings of $3.46 a share, compared with $3.11 a year ago. Share repurchases have helped earnings per share figures, with the company having bought back 8.1 million shares of about a 20 million share repurchase program by June 30. The company had a weighted average of 193.6 million shares outstanding in the first six months of 1996, down from 199.9 million a before.
Caterpillar is expected to also give its first outlook for 1997, with some analysts looking for a projection of some sales gains.
"I would say they probably look for sales to be up in '97 over '96," said Barry Bannister, analyst at S.G. Warburg. "By that I would mean somewhere in the range of five percent at most."
He said he expects Caterpillar to forecast a modest rebound in European markets and a slight slowdown in the Asia-Pacific region, except in Japan.
